First, fetch the existing Jira issue details using the issue ID provided and analyze the current description, comments, and any existing requirements.

**CRITICAL: You MUST format the entire output using JIRA markdown syntax (see JIRA Markdown Format Requirements below). DO NOT use standard markdown or GitHub markdown.**

Then, generate a comprehensive Jira specification that enhances the existing issue with:

1. **Acceptance Criteria** (Product Owner Perspective)
   - User story in proper format (if not already present)
   - Given-When-Then scenarios for all flows (primary, alternative, edge cases)
   - Functional and non-functional requirements
   - Business rules and constraints
   - Error handling and edge cases
   - UX/UI considerations
   - Definition of Done checklist
   - Dependencies and risks

2. **Test Cases** (QA Engineer Perspective)
   - Complete test case specifications with IDs
   - Positive test scenarios (happy path)
   - Negative test scenarios (error handling)
   - Boundary value tests
   - Edge cases and security tests
   - Non-functional tests (performance, security, accessibility, usability)
   - Regression and integration tests
   - Automation recommendations (YES/NO/PARTIAL) with rationale
   - Playwright code examples for automatable tests
   - Test data requirements and test coverage summary

3. **Technical Requirements** (Senior Rails Developer Perspective)
   - Architecture and design patterns selection
   - Database schema changes with zero-downtime migrations
   - API endpoints specification (if applicable) with request/response formats
   - Service objects and business logic organization
   - Background jobs and async processing requirements
   - Performance optimization strategies (query optimization, caching, scalability)
   - Security considerations (authentication, authorization, data protection, input validation)
   - Third-party integrations and webhook handling
   - Error handling and structured logging strategy
   - Code organization structure (services, queries, forms, decorators, policies)
   - Comprehensive testing strategy with RSpec examples (models, services, controllers, jobs)
   - Deployment and rollback considerations with feature flags

**Usage:**
Provide the Jira issue ID (e.g., PROJ-123 or just 123)

**Process:**
1. Fetch the issue details from Jira
2. Analyze existing description, requirements, and context
3. Generate comprehensive specifications based on the issue
4. Format output in **JIRA markdown format** (NOT GitHub/CommonMark markdown) - see examples below
5. Include sections for Acceptance Criteria, Test Cases, and Technical Requirements
6. Attempt to update the Jira issue
7. **If update fails:** Save the generated specification to `/tmp/jira-update-{issue-id}-{timestamp}.md` instead of the root folder

**JIRA Markdown Format Requirements:**
- Headings: `h1.` `h2.` `h3.` `h4.` `h5.` `h6.` (NOT #)
- Bold: `*bold text*` (NOT **)
- Italic: `_italic text_` (NOT *)
- Bullet lists: `*` for bullets, `#` for numbered lists (NOT -)
- Code blocks: `{code:language}...{code}` (NOT ```)
- Inline code: `{{text}}` (NOT backticks)
- Links: `[text|url]` (NOT [text](url))
- Tables: `||heading 1||heading 2||` and `|cell 1|cell 2|`
- Quotes: `{quote}text{quote}` (NOT >)
- Panels: `{panel:title=Title}content{panel}`
- Color: `{color:red}text{color}`
- Line break: Use actual line breaks or `\\`

**JIRA Format Example (User Story Section):**
{code}
h1. User Story

*As a* business customer
*I want to* view the new Platinum Hub homepage
*So that I* can explore Platinum Business products and access role-specific features

h1. Design Reference

* Figma Design: [Design Link|https://www.figma.com/design/example]
* Icon Assets: [Google Drive|https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example]

h1. Acceptance Criteria

h2. AC1: Page Layout and Branding

*Given* a user visits the Platinum Hub homepage
*When* the page loads
*Then* the following elements should be visible:

* IM3 Platinum Business Vertical logo in upper left corner
* "What is Platinum Business" section in left upper corner
* Header navigation with: Toko, Platinum Business, Academy, Wawasan
* Login button OR user icon (if authenticated) in header above banner
* Hero banner on upper right
* Footer with Indosat logo
* Contact email: {{platinumbusiness@ioh.co.id}} in footer
* Social media links pointing to IM3 official channels
{code}

**REMEMBER:**
- Start headings with `h1.` `h2.` etc (with a period and space)
- Use `*text*` for bold (single asterisks)
- Use `_text_` for italic (single underscores)
- Use `{{text}}` for inline code (double curly braces)
- Use `*` at the start of lines for bullet points

**Error Handling:**
- If the Jira update fails (network issues, permissions, etc.), save the generated content to `/tmp/jira-update-{issue-id}-{timestamp}.md`
- Inform the user of the file location so they can manually update Jira or retry later
- Preserve all generated content to avoid data loss

The output will be comprehensive, actionable, and ready for the development team to implement. Each section will be properly formatted for Jira markdown syntax.

Current Issue Description

Please fill column SIM card with no of MSISDN orders on downloaded Excel from Kelola Report as Admin

_Current Behavior:_
The "SIM CARD" column in the order export Excel shows only the first MSISDN number from the order's postpaid activations. For orders with multiple MSISDNs (bulk orders), the current implementation only displays one MSISDN number, making it impossible to see the total count of MSISDNs in an order.

---

h1. 1. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (Product Owner Perspective)

h2. User Story

_As an_ Admin user
_I want to_ see the total count of MSISDN numbers for each order in the Excel export
_So that_ I can quickly understand order size and track bulk order volumes without opening individual orders

h2. Given-When-Then Scenarios

h3. AC-1: Single MSISDN Order Display

_Given_ an order has exactly 1 postpaid activation with 1 MSISDN
_When_ the admin downloads the order report as Excel
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should display "1" (the count)
_And_ the format should be consistent with other numeric columns

h3. AC-2: Multiple MSISDN Order Display (Bulk Orders)

_Given_ an order has multiple postpaid activations (e.g., 5 MSISDNs)
_When_ the admin downloads the order report as Excel
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should display "5" (the total count)
_And_ the count should include all postpaid activations associated with the order

h3. AC-3: Order Without MSISDN Display

_Given_ an order has no postpaid activations assigned yet
_When_ the admin downloads the order report as Excel
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should display "0" or "-"
_And_ the cell should not be empty

h3. AC-4: Excel Formatting

_Given_ the Excel file is generated with MSISDN counts
_When_ the file is opened in Excel or Google Sheets
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should be formatted as a number (not text)
_And_ the column should support sorting and filtering as numeric data
_And_ the column should be right-aligned for better readability

h3. AC-5: Filtered Export Consistency

_Given_ the admin applies filters (search, status, sort) before exporting
_When_ the Excel report is generated
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column counts should match the filtered order data
_And_ all filtered orders should have accurate MSISDN counts

h3. AC-6: Column Header Update

_Given_ the Excel export is generated
_When_ viewing the Excel file
_Then_ the column header should be renamed from "SIM CARD" to "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT"
_And_ the header should be clear and professional in both English and Indonesian

h2. Functional Requirements

# _MSISDN Count Calculation:_ Count all postpaid activations associated with each order through order_items. Include both parent and child postpaid activations in the count. Handle orders with zero activations gracefully.

# _Column Positioning:_ The "NO OF MSISDN" column should remain in the same position (column 7). Maintain consistent column ordering with existing export structure.

# _Data Format:_ Export as numeric value (integer). Support Excel numeric operations (SUM, AVERAGE, etc.). Right-align for consistency with numeric data.

# _Performance:_ Maintain existing query performance with eager loading. Add necessary includes to prevent N+1 queries. Handle large datasets (1000+ orders) efficiently.

# _Bilingual Support:_ Update column header in both Indonesian and English locale files. Suggested translations: English: "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT", Indonesian: "JUMLAH MSISDN" or "JML NOMOR"

h2. Non-Functional Requirements

# _Performance:_ Export generation should complete within 30 seconds for 1000 orders

# _Compatibility:_ Excel file should open correctly in Excel 2016+, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice

# _Data Accuracy:_ MSISDN counts must be 100% accurate across all order types

# _Scalability:_ Solution should handle orders with up to 100 MSISDNs per order

# _Maintainability:_ Code should follow existing service patterns in the codebase

h2. Business Rules and Constraints

# Only postpaid activations with valid MSISDN associations should be counted

# Cancelled or deleted postpaid activations should not be included in the count

# The count should reflect the current state at export time, not historical data

# Orders in "customer_stage" status should not be included in the export (existing behavior)

h2. Error Handling and Edge Cases

|| Scenario || Expected Behavior ||  
| Order with null postpaid_activations | Display "0" |  
| Order with soft-deleted activations | Exclude from count |  
| Order with mixed parent/child activations | Count all activations |  
| Database query timeout | Return error with retry option |  
| Empty result set | Generate Excel with headers only |  
| Invalid order data | Skip invalid records, log error |

h2. Definition of Done

* MSISDN count column displays accurate count for all order types
* Excel file formatting is correct (numeric, right-aligned)
* Column header updated in both EN and ID locales
* Unit tests pass with 100% coverage for new/modified code
* Integration tests verify Excel generation with various scenarios
* Code reviewed and approved by senior developer
* No N+1 query issues introduced
* Performance benchmarks meet requirements (<30s for 1000 orders)
* Documentation updated (if needed)
* QA testing completed successfully
* Deployed to staging environment and verified
* Product Owner acceptance received

h2. Dependencies and Risks

_Dependencies:_

* Existing Order and PostpaidActivation models
* Export::OrderExportService service
* Admin::OrdersController#export_xls action
* Locale files for translations

_Risks:_

* _Medium Risk:_ Performance degradation with large datasets - _Mitigation:_ Use counter_cache or optimize query with includes
* _Low Risk:_ Breaking existing Excel parsing in downstream systems - _Mitigation:_ Keep column position same, only change content
* _Low Risk:_ Translation inconsistency between platforms - _Mitigation:_ Review with bilingual team member

* KISS: Simple count query, no over-engineering

Current Issue Description

Please fill column SIM card with no of MSISDN orders on downloaded Excel from Kelola Report as Admin

_Current Behavior:_
The "SIM CARD" column in the order export Excel shows only the first MSISDN number from the order's postpaid activations. For orders with multiple MSISDNs (bulk orders), the current implementation only displays one MSISDN number, making it impossible to see the total count of MSISDNs in an order.

---

h1. 1. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (Product Owner Perspective)

h2. User Story

_As an_ Admin user
_I want to_ see the total count of MSISDN numbers for each order in the Excel export
_So that_ I can quickly understand order size and track bulk order volumes without opening individual orders

h2. Given-When-Then Scenarios

h3. AC-1: Single MSISDN Order Display

_Given_ an order has exactly 1 postpaid activation with 1 MSISDN
_When_ the admin downloads the order report as Excel
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should display "1" (the count)
_And_ the format should be consistent with other numeric columns

h3. AC-2: Multiple MSISDN Order Display (Bulk Orders)

_Given_ an order has multiple postpaid activations (e.g., 5 MSISDNs)
_When_ the admin downloads the order report as Excel
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should display "5" (the total count)
_And_ the count should include all postpaid activations associated with the order

h3. AC-3: Order Without MSISDN Display

_Given_ an order has no postpaid activations assigned yet
_When_ the admin downloads the order report as Excel
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should display "0" or "-"
_And_ the cell should not be empty

h3. AC-4: Excel Formatting

_Given_ the Excel file is generated with MSISDN counts
_When_ the file is opened in Excel or Google Sheets
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column should be formatted as a number (not text)
_And_ the column should support sorting and filtering as numeric data
_And_ the column should be right-aligned for better readability

h3. AC-5: Filtered Export Consistency

_Given_ the admin applies filters (search, status, sort) before exporting
_When_ the Excel report is generated
_Then_ the "SIM CARD" column counts should match the filtered order data
_And_ all filtered orders should have accurate MSISDN counts

h3. AC-6: Column Header Update

_Given_ the Excel export is generated
_When_ viewing the Excel file
_Then_ the column header should be renamed from "SIM CARD" to "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT"
_And_ the header should be clear and professional in both English and Indonesian

h2. Functional Requirements

# _MSISDN Count Calculation:_ Count all postpaid activations associated with each order through order_items. Include both parent and child postpaid activations in the count. Handle orders with zero activations gracefully.

# _Column Positioning:_ The "NO OF MSISDN" column should remain in the same position (column 7). Maintain consistent column ordering with existing export structure.

# _Data Format:_ Export as numeric value (integer). Support Excel numeric operations (SUM, AVERAGE, etc.). Right-align for consistency with numeric data.

# _Performance:_ Maintain existing query performance with eager loading. Add necessary includes to prevent N+1 queries. Handle large datasets (1000+ orders) efficiently.

# _Bilingual Support:_ Update column header in both Indonesian and English locale files. Suggested translations: English: "NO OF MSISDN" or "MSISDN COUNT", Indonesian: "JUMLAH MSISDN" or "JML NOMOR"

h2. Non-Functional Requirements

# _Performance:_ Export generation should complete within 30 seconds for 1000 orders

# _Compatibility:_ Excel file should open correctly in Excel 2016+, Google Sheets, and LibreOffice

# _Data Accuracy:_ MSISDN counts must be 100% accurate across all order types

# _Scalability:_ Solution should handle orders with up to 100 MSISDNs per order

# _Maintainability:_ Code should follow existing service patterns in the codebase

h2. Business Rules and Constraints

# Only postpaid activations with valid MSISDN associations should be counted

# Cancelled or deleted postpaid activations should not be included in the count

# The count should reflect the current state at export time, not historical data

# Orders in "customer_stage" status should not be included in the export (existing behavior)

h2. Error Handling and Edge Cases

|| Scenario || Expected Behavior ||  
| Order with null postpaid_activations | Display "0" |  
| Order with soft-deleted activations | Exclude from count |  
| Order with mixed parent/child activations | Count all activations |  
| Database query timeout | Return error with retry option |  
| Empty result set | Generate Excel with headers only |  
| Invalid order data | Skip invalid records, log error |

h2. Definition of Done

* MSISDN count column displays accurate count for all order types
* Excel file formatting is correct (numeric, right-aligned)
* Column header updated in both EN and ID locales
* Unit tests pass with 100% coverage for new/modified code
* Integration tests verify Excel generation with various scenarios
* Code reviewed and approved by senior developer
* No N+1 query issues introduced
* Performance benchmarks meet requirements (<30s for 1000 orders)
* Documentation updated (if needed)
* QA testing completed successfully
* Deployed to staging environment and verified
* Product Owner acceptance received

h2. Dependencies and Risks

_Dependencies:_

* Existing Order and PostpaidActivation models
* Export::OrderExportService service
* Admin::OrdersController#export_xls action
* Locale files for translations

_Risks:_

* _Medium Risk:_ Performance degradation with large datasets - _Mitigation:_ Use counter_cache or optimize query with includes
* _Low Risk:_ Breaking existing Excel parsing in downstream systems - _Mitigation:_ Keep column position same, only change content
* _Low Risk:_ Translation inconsistency between platforms - _Mitigation:_ Review with bilingual team member

* KISS: Simple count query, no over-engineering

Optional performance optimization: Consider adding counter cache if N+1 queries become an issue with large datasets.

h2. Service Objects and Business Logic

_Changes Required:_

if order.postpaid_activations.loaded?

h2. Controller Changes

@orders = Order.where.not(regular_user: nil)

  )  
{code}

_Rationale:_ This ensures postpaid_activations are eager loaded, preventing N+1 queries.
